name: African American and African Studies
department: Carter G. Woodson Institute for African-American and African Studies

requirements.label: Introductory core (grade C or better in each)
Electives (12 credits)
requirements.note: Twelve credits beyond AAS 1010/1020 from the list of approved courses posted on the Woodson Institute website; approved courses in other departments (e.g. HIAF, HIUS, ENGL, MUSI cross-lists) also count but the list was not available.

notes: Minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses counted toward the minor. Up to 6 credits of relevant study abroad may count with prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Programs. Approved non-AAS electives are not modelled.

name: African Studies
department: Carter G. Woodson Institute for African-American and African Studies

requirements.label: Required history of Africa (grade C or better in each)
Approved electives (12 credits)
requirements.note: Twelve additional credits approved by the Director of Undergraduate Programs; Africa-focused courses in other departments (anthropology, French, politics, religious studies, African languages, etc.) can be approved. Not every AAS course is Africa-focused.

notes: Six courses totaling at least 20 credits, taken from at least two departments. Minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses counted toward the minor. Up to 6 credits of relevant study abroad may apply. Elective approval is case-by-case and not fully modelled.

name: Southern Studies

declaration.notes: Consult the director (Grace Hale) before declaring; declare with the general Minor Declaration Form.

requirements.label: Electives (four)
requirements.note: Electives may come from the core list or from a semester-by-semester list of approved Southern-content courses across AMST, AAS, History, English, Politics, Religious Studies, WGS and others. Only approved courses count; subject wildcards are approximations. Courses used for the core cannot be reused here.

notes: Six courses / 18 credits. At most one course taken outside UVA (study abroad or transfer). College double-counting rules apply. No minimum grade stated on the page.

name: Art History

requirements.label: Prerequisite: Art Worlds (grade C or above)

declaration.notes: Contact the Director of the Undergraduate Program to be assigned an advisor, then submit the College Declare a Major/Minor form.

requirements.label: Art Worlds
requirements.note: Gateway course; assumed to count as one of the 10 courses.

requirements.label: Distribution: before 1500 (2000-level or above)
requirements.note: Lists on the department page are examples; other approved courses may count.

requirements.label: Distribution: African, Asian, or Indigenous traditions
Capstones: two 4000-level courses
requirements.note: Seminars, Arts Administration, DMP preparation, or advanced topics. Cannot also satisfy a distribution requirement.

requirements.label: Two additional courses at 3000 level or above
requirements.note: May overlap with other requirements (distribution), but not with the two capstones.

requirements.label: Total: 10 courses
requirements.note: At least 9 above the 1000 level. At most one 1000-level ARTH course (AP 4/5 counts) and at most one Studio Art (ARTS) course. Architectural History (ARH) at 2000+ and ARAD coursework count.

notes: No course graded below C- counts; ARTH 2000 needs C or above. Major GPA of at least 2.000 by graduation. One course cannot satisfy more than one distribution requirement. Pre-1500, post-1500, and African/Asian/Indigenous are three separate distribution requirements (the minor page confirms 'three requirements'); a cross-listed course like ARTH 2961 appears on several lists but can satisfy only one. Transfer, dual-enrollment, study-abroad credit counts. Credits assume 3-credit courses (10 courses ~30 credits).

name: Studio Art

declaration.notes: Complete the Major Declaration Form (DocuSign) and meet with the studio advisor (A-L: Federico Cuatlacuatl; M-Z: Neal Rock). Since Fall 2024 ARTS 2000 is no longer required to enter upper-division courses.

requirements.label: Studio courses at 2000-level or above (12 credits)
Concentration (9 credits in ONE concentration, at least 3 at 3000-level)
requirements.note: All 9 credits must be in a single concentration: Digital Art (ARTS 22xx/32xx/42xx 220,222), Filmmaking (x370, x372), Painting (x710, x712), Photography (x110, x112), Printmaking (x670, x672), Sculpture (x810, x812). At least 3 of the 9 credits at the 3000 level. Special Topics courses do not count toward the concentration. Single-concentration rule is not enforced by this group.

requirements.label: Modern/contemporary art history
requirements.note: Spring 2027 list from the department; the approved list changes each term.

notes: 30 credits; groups are intended to be filled by distinct courses (12 + 9 + 3 + 3 + 3). Minimum 2.000 GPA in the 30 major credits; C- or below does not count. Up to 9 transfer credits with DUP approval. ARTS 4450/4452 (Advanced Major Seminar, year-long, 4th year) and ARTS 4900 do not count toward the 30 credits; the seminar is required for the Distinguished Majors Program (expected 3.4 GPA, thesis exhibition). Students planning a thesis show must be in a 4000-level class in their final semester. Painting courses require ARTS 2610 (Drawing I); the exact painting course numbers needing it are assumed (ARTS 2710/2712).

name: Studio Art

requirements.label: At least 15 credits at 2000-level or above, in at least two concentration areas
requirements.note: Must span at least two concentration areas (Digital Art, Filmmaking, Painting, Photography, Printmaking, Sculpture); not enforced here. At least one course must be at the 2000 level (implied by this group).

notes: Minimum 2.000 GPA across the 18 minor credits; no ARTS course graded C- or below counts. ARTS 4900 does not count. Up to 6 transfer credits with DUP approval.
